items.stem: Why is holding a std::sync::Mutex guard across an .await point in async Rust a problem?

options.text: The task may be suspended while holding the lock, blocking other tasks and risking deadlock
options.rationale: Correct: the guard is held across suspension, so other tasks waiting on the lock stall; an async-aware mutex is preferred.

options.text: std mutexes cannot compile in async code at all
options.rationale: They compile; the problem is holding the guard across await.

options.text: It automatically converts to an async mutex
options.rationale: No automatic conversion happens; the risk remains.
It does not improve performance; it creates a hazard.

items.explanation: Correct: the guard is held across suspension, so other tasks waiting on the lock stall; an async-aware mutex is preferred.

items.stem: Which are sound resilience practices for an async service under load? (Select TWO)

options.text: Apply timeouts so slow dependencies cannot stall requests indefinitely
options.rationale: Correct: timeouts bound how long a request waits on a dependency.

options.text: Bound concurrency so the service sheds or queues load instead of collapsing
options.rationale: Correct: backpressure protects the service from being overwhelmed.

options.text: Retry immediately and unboundedly on every failure
options.rationale: Unbounded immediate retries amplify an outage; use backoff and limits.

options.text: Return full internal stack traces to every client
options.rationale: Leaking internals is a security and clarity problem.

items.explanation: Correct: timeouts bound how long a request waits on a dependency.; Correct: backpressure protects the service from being overwhelmed.

items.stem: What does spawning a tokio task with tokio::spawn require of the task's data, and why?

options.text: The future must be Send so it can run on the multi-threaded runtime's worker threads
options.rationale: Correct: tasks may move between worker threads, so their captured data must be Send.
Copy is not required; Send (and 'static) is.

options.text: Nothing; any data can be captured freely
options.rationale: The Send/'static bounds are real constraints.

options.text: The future must block until completion
options.rationale: Spawned tasks run concurrently; they do not block the spawner.

items.explanation: Correct: tasks may move between worker threads, so their captured data must be Send.
